_comment: The 7 tracked products. Every endpoint here was PROVEN by fetching it during
the receipts. Endpoints that could not be resolved are null, not guessed.
MATCHING RULES (this is the accuracy-critical part):
aliases          - any literal occurrence in fetched page text confirms a mention
require_context  - for ambiguous names ('Confluence', 'Guru'), at least ONE of
these must ALSO appear on the page, or the match is rejected.
Without this, 'a confluence of factors' and 'SEO guru' would
inflate the mention counts and corrupt share-of-voice.
negative_context - if present, the match is rejected outright.

gitbook.name: GitBook
gitbook.blog_feed_note: No discoverable RSS/Atom feed — probed 8 candidate paths plus <head> autodiscovery, all 404. Blog coverage for GitBook comes from SearXNG + GDELT web discovery instead.

confluence.name: Confluence
confluence.ambiguity_note: 'Confluence' is a common English noun. require_context prevents 'a confluence of factors' from being counted as a product mention.
confluence.blog_feed_note: Atlassian's corporate blog covers all products; records are still gated on a confirmed Confluence mention in the fetched text.
confluence.youtube_note: Atlassian's corporate channel — video records require a confirmed Confluence mention in the title or description.
confluence.linkedin_verified_note: HTTP 429 (rate limited) during config verification — existence not proven, treat as unconfirmed.

guru.name: Guru
guru.ambiguity_note: 'Guru' is a common English noun. require_context plus negative_context keeps 'SEO guru' out of the counts.
guru.blog_feed_note: No discoverable RSS/Atom feed — probed 6 candidate paths plus <head> autodiscovery, all 404. Blog coverage comes from SearXNG + GDELT.

knowledgeowl.name: KnowledgeOwl
knowledgeowl.blog_feed_note: No discoverable RSS/Atom feed — probed 9 candidate paths plus <head> autodiscovery, all 404 (one 200 returned HTML, not a feed). Blog coverage comes from SearXNG + GDELT.
knowledgeowl.youtube_note: No YouTube channel resolved for any tried handle. The Videos channel for KnowledgeOwl is populated by SearXNG site:youtube.com discovery instead of an owned-channel feed.

event_sources._comment: Event-sponsorship detection. Sponsorship is rarely in an API, so it is evidence-based: a page must contain the brand name AND a sponsorship term, and the excerpt is retained for audit. Terms are deliberately narrow to avoid counting mere attendance as sponsorship.
